description: Cross-tool context: time per RIS channel evaluation of the same near-field K1 sum (N = 256, 1024, 4096) with sremu (numba, NumPy) and MATLAB R2026a (hand loop, vectorized, toolbox primitives) plus phased.RISReflector (a different, far-field model); copied unchanged

data_class_notes.MEAS: laptop timings (Windows, not quiet: other processes 28 % busy on average during the sremu section)
data_class_notes.REPORTED: literature rows of run/context_table.csv and run/literature.csv (not used as paper numbers)

run.protocol: median of repeated calls per method and N (sremu: n_calls in run/times.csv; MATLAB: timeit in one session, start-up excluded); quiet gate max 20 % busy over 3 s met before the run

choice: the later of two laptop runs: 20261011T024620Z recorded the load as one number (mean 0.91, MATLAB counted as background), had no per-section load and an 82 ms RISReflector outlier at N = 4096 (~178x this run's 0.46 ms); this run has per-section load (run/sections.json) and the same spec hash

host.cores_note: 8 cores / 16 threads (DESIGN 12.4; the manifest records logical CPUs only)

sremu.dirty_note: working tree with uncommitted changes; the patch (sha256 in dirty_patch_sha256) is kept in the authors' archive and not published (it contains internal development notes); B6 is to be re-run at the pinned commit

caveats: Different work per call: the sremu times include Python dispatch and the LOS path; MATLAB times exclude start-up; RISReflector is a different model.
One machine, Windows, with background load: context, not a ranking.
Same-model agreement sremu vs MATLAB: 7.8e-14 dB.
